title: Count Connected Subgraphs with Even Node Sum
summary: Given an undirected graph with nodes labeled from 0 to n-1, where each node has a value of either 0 or 1, count the number of non-empty subsets of nodes such that the induced subgraph is connected and the sum of node values in the subset is even.
statement: Given an undirected graph with nodes labeled from 0 to n-1, where each node has a value of either 0 or 1, count the number of non-empty subsets of nodes such that the induced subgraph is connected and the sum of node values in the subset is even.
constraints: nums contains zero/one node values; edges defines an undirected simple graph.
Choose a nonempty node subset whose induced subgraph is connected.
Count subsets with even value sum.
hints: For the intended small n, enumerate every nonempty node mask.
Reject odd value sums, then run DFS restricted to nodes whose mask bits are set.
Count the mask only when DFS reaches every selected node.
Every induced subset has one mask and connectivity is exactly restricted reachability, so enumeration is complete without duplicates.
editorial: Every induced subset has one mask and connectivity is exactly restricted reachability, so enumeration is complete without duplicates.

tests.explanation: The singleton zero node and the full connected path with sum two are the two qualifying subsets.
The single zero-valued node is connected and has even sum, so the answer is one.
